#termmax @termmax  前几天在 @termmax 体验了一把当债主，本打算舒舒服服吃个 9% 的年化利息。放出去的是硬通货 USDC，想着到期连本带利收回，妥妥的无脑理财。谁料借钱那哥们在第 25 天居然不还钱了！更离谱的是，系统直接往我地址里打了一堆 PT-sUSDe。原来这平台搞的是“以物抵债”（physical delivery），坏账了不负责卖货，直接把质押物强塞给资金方。

按以前在 Aave 或者 Compound 的经验，遇到烂账，清算机器人会立刻去竞价抛售。出资方拿回来的依然是稳定币，顶多承担 5% 的清算罚款。但在 TermMax 这里，压根没有竞价环节。这套玩法对那些没啥交易量、脱手极难的标的（比如 RWA 或 tokenized stock）确实管用。但这等于是把“套现难”的黑锅，从协议端完美转移到了咱们散户头上。

掏出计算器一敲，心都凉了。拿到那批 PT-sUSDe 时，盘面价已经跌破面值 1.8%。更要命的是，距离最终兑付还有足足 18 天。我去 DEX 瞄了一眼，池子浅得令人发指，稍微抛一点就会砸出 3% 的滑点！强行变现不仅白干，还要倒贴 Gas 费。但要是死等，这 18 天的空窗期里，万一 sUSDe 对应的底层协议出点幺蛾子，我连割肉跑路的机会都没有。

这波纯属用真金白银交了学费。以后去 TermMax 赚收益，千万别被利率蒙蔽双眼。掏钱前先扪心自问：如果对面爆仓了，你愿不愿意抱着他的资产过夜？如果不想，这单就别碰。这套交割机制对项目方来说确实是个 feature，但背后的流动性深坑，全凭咱们自己硬扛。#eth $ETH

title: Don't Just Do Your Research. Challenge It.
subTitle:
Doing research doesn't mean collecting information that supports what you already believe. That's confirmation bias. Real research should challenge your assumptions. If you believe a project has strong potential, ask:
🔹 What could make this project fail?
🔹 What are its biggest weaknesses?
🔹 Who are its strongest competitors?
🔹 Is the token actually necessary?
🔹 What happens if adoption doesn't grow?
🔹 What would make me change my mind?
The goal isn't to prove yourself right. The goal is to discover whether your thesis can survive serious questions.
🔑 Key Takeaway: Research that only confirms your belief isn't research. It's reassurance. A strong investment thesis should survive both the bull case and the bear case.
🧠 Practical Reflection; Before your next investment, write down two things: Why could this investment succeed Then ask: Why could I be completely wrong? If you cannot answer the second question, your research may not be finished.
Thought for the Day. Don't research to find reasons to buy. Research to discover whether buying actually makes sense.
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Earlier, in a coffee shop, I was chatting idly with a coworker. I thought I’d show off a bit about the underlying logic of blockchain—only for him to throw out a tricky question right away. Their company plans to move a chunk of institutional assets onto the chain. The bottom line is not only to satisfy official audit requirements, but also to prevent competitors from peeking at their cards. At that moment, I was completely stunned. In the crypto space, hasn’t the supposed “deal” between anonymity and compliance always been an unsolvable knot?

With a head full of doubts, I went to get a deep primer on <t-2/> Dusk Network, an L1 blockchain that focuses on financial confidentiality. After going through the materials, I found that the most core, hard-hitting weapon is the Phoenix UTXO architecture. You see, with Ethereum’s old-school account model, transfers are basically like running around in the nude—you can trace everything by following the trail. Dusk counters this with a one-two punch: Nullifiers (spent/obsolete markers) combined with a Merkle tree. I even walked through the testnet and tried contract deployment and payments. What I found was that it doesn’t expose the “thickness” of your wallet or who the recipient is. The system simply takes the amount you used to generate a dedicated hash and drops it into a nullifier pool, then packages the newly received funds into a new node on the Merkle tree.

I have to say, this stealth technique really has two moves. Outsiders can’t piece together the in-and-out flow of funds. With that, major institutions no longer have to worry about robots intercepting their positions while building their stakes.

But the problem spots are just as glaring.

After interacting with it myself, the side effects of this mechanism drove me crazy. Because every on-chain action requires generating a zero-knowledge proof locally and then validating the Nullifier, even though the project team specifically tinkered with Piecrust zkVM to speed things up, in real use those seconds of proving delay caused by client-side computation are unbearable for players who are used to near-instant, second-level responsiveness.

Personally, I think Dusk’s attempt to swallow the big pie of compliance-oriented privacy and real-world assets (RWA) is definitely a compelling story. But market survival never trades in fairy tales. With current policy directions being extremely strict, a “selective disclosure” chain can, with one misstep, trigger the risk controls of major firms and get forced offline. So here’s a heads-up for the project team: if you want the ecosystem to have a steady flow of users, don’t just obsess over lofty capital. #dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Last weekend, I met up with a friend for tea. I planned to discuss blockchain’s underlying layer with him—but this brother came back with a god-level request: their firm intends to move some assets on-chain, with the condition that they can’t just keep the doors open to the authorities, they also have to lock down transaction details so tightly competitors can’t get a thing. After hearing it, I was like, “Well, damn!” In the crypto world, isn’t anonymity and compliance supposed to be a case of no harm done to each other? 

With doubts in my mind, I did an in-depth investigation into Dusk Network, an L1 chain focused on financial privacy. After chewing through the materials, I found that the hardest-core ace up its sleeve is the Phoenix UTXO architecture. As everyone knows, Ethereum’s traditional account model is basically “running around in the nude” when you transfer funds. Dusk, on the other hand, uses Nullifier plus a Merkle tree mechanism. I ran it through the testnet and tried making payments and executing contracts. What’s impressive is that when you submit a transaction, it doesn’t expose your inputs or the recipient. The system simply takes the spent amount, generates an independent hash, throws it into a discard pool, and then turns the new funds into hidden nodes.

This logic really has something to it! Outsiders can’t figure out the upstream and downstream of the money flow, and big players finally don’t have to worry about their positions being front-run by machines.

But every story has a cost. In practice, the biggest pain point is: stuttering.

Because every time the state refreshes, it forces the local client to run zero-knowledge proofs and verify the Nullifier. Although the Dusk team has been tinkering with a dedicated Piecrust zkVM to speed things up, the few seconds of generation delay are still hard to ignore. Once you’re used to the smooth operations you normally get, sacrificing fluidity just to stay hidden really does hurt the experience.

Dusk wants to package the benefits of institutional-level RWA and compliant privacy—sounds tempting. But the market has never looked at technology alone. Now policy strings are getting tight; privacy chains built on “selective transparency” have a real risk of being taken down by mainstream platforms at any moment. Honestly, I’d advise Dusk one thing: take more care of regular retail users’ feelings, and don’t just keep staring at the giants. If no retail users are there to support the stage, even the sexiest vision will eventually turn cold.#eth $ETH

I can’t believe I took that silent loss—I just kept slapping my thigh in frustration! 

For the sake of stability, I went and looked into the project @TermMax. Honestly, the Range Order that TMX loudly claims to be its biggest feature does have something to it. The玩法 (mechanics) is quite similar to Uni V3’s concentrated liquidity. We can set conditions within our preferred APR range for automatic matching, and it even supports one-click looping with leverage. 

With a try-it-out mindset, I watched the charts and ran it for almost a month. The sweet spot of this system is that it lays out your profits clearly and cleanly. Back then I put in a bit of ETH, minted GT, then sold off FT in a handoff, and used it to borrow 2,000 USDC to place a trade with a 14-day cycle. The underlying model called TermMaxCurve is extremely forceful—it essentially locked my annualized return at 5.8%. Over the next few days, I felt at ease checking parameters and assembling parts in the workshop. I didn’t have to keep grabbing my phone every few days to check live quotes like I have some kind of obsessive-compulsive disorder. 

But there’s no such thing as a free lunch. Only after you wade into the water do you learn how deep the traps really go. Many people don’t realize that TermMax’s secondary order book is extremely weak right now—maybe the hype hasn’t caught up yet. A while back I needed money urgently, so I wanted to liquidate my FT early at a discount. What happened? Because of the AMM model combined with a sadly thin number of posted orders on the book, the trading slippage was absolutely outrageous, wiping out nearly 30% of my expected interest. When I saw the statement, I almost spewed out an old mouthful of blood. 

What really messes with your head is this: when you click that one-click leverage feature, the system’s underlying Router has to run several smart contracts back and forth. Each interaction burns Gas like crazy. For small retail folks like us who don’t have a huge principal, don’t touch it. 

All in all, TMX, by using FT, GT, and range order mechanisms, really does bring some new flavors to the fixed-income circle. But until market-making capital and liquidity gaps are filled, the cost of bailing out mid-way is just too brutal. Guys, if you’re planning to jump in, please—don’t go all-in at once! #eth $ETH
